demos.title: Atomic commits & failure isolation
demos.summary: A Spark job dies half-way through an append. Readers never see a partial write.
demos.why: In Iceberg a write becomes visible only when the catalog atomically swaps the table's metadata pointer. Data files that tasks wrote before the job failed are not referenced by any snapshot, so readers never see them — they are 'orphans' in storage, exactly like files left by a killed driver, and orphan-file cleanup removes them.

steps.label: Committed state before the failing job
Append of 8 partitions; partition 5 throws
steps.sql: df.repartition(8)...writeTo(t).append()

steps.label: Simulated hard crash leaves an uncommitted file in storage
Storage listing vs. files referenced by any snapshot
steps.sql: files under data/  MINUS  SELECT file_path FROM lab.acid_orders.all_files

steps.label: DeleteOrphanFiles action removes it
steps.sql: SparkActions.get(spark).deleteOrphanFiles(table).olderThan(now).execute()

demos.title: Time travel
demos.summary: Query silver.orders exactly as it was after each incremental batch — from Spark and from DuckDB.
demos.why: Every commit is an immutable snapshot. VERSION AS OF / TIMESTAMP AS OF read an old snapshot's manifests, so historical queries are exact and need no copies or audit tables.

steps.label: Status mix: first snapshot vs current
steps.sql: SELECT coalesce(a.order_status, b.order_status) AS order_status, a.n AS first_snapshot, b.n AS current FROM (SELECT order_status, count(*) n FROM lake.silver.orders VERSION AS OF 5333925609465049315 GROUP BY 1) a FULL OUTER JOIN (SELECT order_status, count(*) n FROM lake.silver.orders GROUP BY 1) b ON a.order_status = b.order_status ORDER BY current DESC NULLS LAST

steps.label: One order's life across snapshots (056793caf884…)
steps.sql: SELECT order_status FROM silver.orders VERSION AS OF <id> WHERE order_id = '056793caf8844dea629fd51221dda31d'

steps.label: TIMESTAMP AS OF works the same way
steps.sql: SELECT count(*) AS orders FROM lake.silver.orders TIMESTAMP AS OF '2026-11-12 00:52:35.237'

steps.label: Same snapshots read by DuckDB (no Spark)
steps.sql: SELECT count(*) FROM lake.silver.orders AT (VERSION => <snapshot_id>)  -- DuckDB

demos.title: Schema evolution
demos.summary: Add, rename, widen and drop columns without rewriting a single data file.
demos.why: Iceberg identifies columns by ID, not by name or position. Schema changes are metadata commits; old files are read through the new schema (new columns read as NULL), and old snapshots keep their own schema for time travel.

steps.label: Add a column
steps.sql: ALTER TABLE lake.lab.customers_evolution ADD COLUMN loyalty_tier STRING COMMENT 'gold/silver/bronze'

steps.label: Rename a column
steps.sql: ALTER TABLE lake.lab.customers_evolution RENAME COLUMN customer_city TO city

steps.label: Widen INT -> BIGINT
steps.sql: ALTER TABLE lake.lab.customers_evolution ALTER COLUMN orders_count TYPE BIGINT

steps.label: Widen FLOAT -> DOUBLE
steps.sql: ALTER TABLE lake.lab.customers_evolution ALTER COLUMN lifetime_value TYPE DOUBLE

steps.label: Move a column
steps.sql: ALTER TABLE lake.lab.customers_evolution ALTER COLUMN loyalty_tier AFTER customer_id

steps.label: Drop a column
steps.sql: ALTER TABLE lake.lab.customers_evolution DROP COLUMN customer_state

steps.label: Data files rewritten by the six schema changes
Backfill the new column (a normal row-level write)
steps.sql: UPDATE lake.lab.customers_evolution SET loyalty_tier = CASE WHEN lifetime_value >= 500 THEN 'gold' WHEN lifetime_value >= 150 THEN 'silver' ELSE 'bronze' END

steps.label: Current snapshot through the new schema
steps.sql: SELECT customer_id, loyalty_tier, city, orders_count, lifetime_value FROM lake.lab.customers_evolution ORDER BY lifetime_value DESC LIMIT 3

steps.label: Time travel to the first snapshot returns the original schema
steps.sql: SELECT * FROM lab.customers_evolution VERSION AS OF 5107050580306302225

demos.title: Partition evolution & hidden partitioning
demos.summary: Start with monthly partitions, switch new data to daily partitions — no rewrite, one table.
demos.why: Partitions are derived from column values by transforms (months(ts), days(ts), bucket(n, id)). Queries filter on the column itself; Iceberg maps predicates to partitions for every spec the table has ever had, so old and new layouts coexist.

steps.label: Load history with spec 0: months(order_purchase_timestamp)
steps.sql: INSERT INTO lake.lab.orders_partitioning SELECT order_id, customer_id, order_status, order_purchase_timestamp FROM lake.silver.orders WHERE order_purchase_timestamp < '2018-09-01'

steps.label: Evolve the spec: monthly -> daily
steps.sql: ALTER TABLE lake.lab.orders_partitioning REPLACE PARTITION FIELD order_purchase_timestamp_month WITH days(order_purchase_timestamp)

steps.label: New data lands with spec 1: days(order_purchase_timestamp)
steps.sql: INSERT INTO lake.lab.orders_partitioning SELECT order_id, customer_id, order_status, order_purchase_timestamp FROM lake.silver.orders WHERE order_purchase_timestamp >= '2018-09-01'

steps.label: Files per partition spec
steps.sql: SELECT spec_id, count(*) AS data_files, count(DISTINCT partition) AS partitions, sum(record_count) AS records FROM lake.lab.orders_partitioning.files GROUP BY spec_id ORDER BY spec_id

steps.label: Partitions table (sample)
steps.sql: SELECT partition, spec_id, record_count, file_count FROM lake.lab.orders_partitioning.partitions ORDER BY spec_id DESC, record_count DESC

steps.label: One query spans both layouts — filter on the column, not on a partition column
steps.sql: SELECT date_format(order_purchase_timestamp, 'yyyy-MM') AS month, count(*) AS orders FROM lake.lab.orders_partitioning WHERE order_purchase_timestamp >= '2018-08-15' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

demos.title: Rollback after a bad deploy
demos.summary: A buggy job multiplies order values by 100. Tag, inspect, roll back — in seconds.
demos.why: rollback_to_snapshot only moves the current-snapshot pointer, so recovery is instant and needs no backups. The bad snapshot stays in history for investigation until it is expired.

steps.label: Known-good state (tagged 'before-bad-deploy')
steps.sql: SELECT round(sum(order_value), 2) AS revenue, round(avg(order_value), 2) AS avg_order_value FROM lake.lab.fact_orders_rollback

steps.label: Bad deploy: a unit bug multiplies 2018 order values by 100
steps.sql: UPDATE lake.lab.fact_orders_rollback SET order_value = order_value * 100 WHERE order_date >= DATE '2018-01-01'

steps.label: Broken state
steps.sql: SELECT round(sum(order_value), 2) AS revenue, round(avg(order_value), 2) AS avg_order_value FROM lake.lab.fact_orders_rollback

steps.label: Snapshots
steps.sql: SELECT snapshot_id, operation, CAST(committed_at AS STRING) AS committed_at FROM lake.lab.fact_orders_rollback.snapshots ORDER BY committed_at

steps.label: Roll back to the tagged snapshot
steps.sql: CALL lake.system.rollback_to_snapshot(table => 'lab.fact_orders_rollback', snapshot_id => 6377109134901611531)

steps.label: Restored state
steps.sql: SELECT round(sum(order_value), 2) AS revenue, round(avg(order_value), 2) AS avg_order_value FROM lake.lab.fact_orders_rollback

steps.label: Tag still points at the good snapshot
steps.sql: SELECT name, type, snapshot_id FROM lake.lab.fact_orders_rollback.refs

demos.title: Write-Audit-Publish with branches
demos.summary: Stage a new day of data on an 'audit' branch, validate it, then publish atomically.
demos.why: Branches are named snapshot lineages. Consumers read 'main' while a job writes to a branch; once quality checks pass, fast_forward publishes the branch to main in one metadata commit.

steps.label: Create the audit branch
steps.sql: ALTER TABLE lake.lab.daily_revenue_wap CREATE BRANCH audit

steps.label: Write tomorrow's data to the branch (with one bad row)
steps.sql: INSERT INTO lake.lab.daily_revenue_wap.branch_audit VALUES (DATE '2018-10-01', 151, 21734.55), (DATE '2018-10-02', 149, -999.0)

steps.label: Audit: revenue must be non-negative
steps.sql: SELECT order_date, revenue FROM lake.lab.daily_revenue_wap VERSION AS OF 'audit' WHERE revenue < 0

steps.label: Fix on the branch
steps.sql: DELETE FROM lake.lab.daily_revenue_wap.branch_audit WHERE revenue < 0

steps.label: Audit again
steps.sql: SELECT count(*) AS failing_rows FROM lake.lab.daily_revenue_wap VERSION AS OF 'audit' WHERE revenue < 0

steps.label: Publish: fast-forward main to audit
steps.sql: CALL lake.system.fast_forward(table => 'lab.daily_revenue_wap', branch => 'main', to => 'audit')

demos.title: Compaction, manifest rewrite & snapshot expiration
demos.summary: 40 micro-batches create 40+ small files and 40 snapshots. Compact, then expire history.
demos.why: Each commit adds files and a snapshot. Many small files slow planning and scanning; rewrite_data_files bin-packs them, and expire_snapshots bounds metadata growth (and how far back time travel can go).

steps.label: rewrite_data_files (bin-pack)
steps.sql: CALL lake.system.rewrite_data_files(table => 'lab.payments_small_files', options => map('min-input-files','2'))

steps.label: rewrite_manifests
steps.sql: CALL lake.system.rewrite_manifests(table => 'lab.payments_small_files')

steps.label: expire_snapshots(retain_last => 3)
steps.sql: CALL lake.system.expire_snapshots(table => 'lab.payments_small_files', older_than => now(), retain_last => 3)
